subject: AWS Private Offer — rate bridge & $/1M token target
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Private Offer — rate bridge & $/1M token target

Hi Samira / AWS team,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the asks we agreed to align on for a private offer mapping: 

Summary of Acme usage profile (per call):
- Expected steady-state inference volume: 5M–20M tokens / month (spikes to ~30M in Q4).
- Workloads: customer-facing summarization + long-form generation (avg seq len ~750 tokens).
- Mix: ~85% generation, ~15% embeddings/rerank.

Acme target economics and asks:
- Target unit: $/1M tokens — Acme is aiming for a target of $1,000 / 1M tokens (ballpark).
- Target monthly budget range: $5k–$20k depending on seasonality.
- Needs to understand how an AWS Private Offer SKU/price can be mapped to Redwood's per-token billing (per-1M token equivalent).

Open questions for AWS:
1) Can AWS marketplace private offers support a custom unit metric mapping to "per 1M tokens" (or will we have to map to an integer SKU unit and apply a conversion factor)?
2) Any limits/rounding rules on unit price precision we should know about (e.g., min increment, currency granularity)?
3) Will the private offer be able to express tiering for volume breaks (e.g., 5M–10M / 10M–25M)?

Next steps I propose:
- Ben / Rishi to draft a mapping table (Redwood per-1M token -> AWS SKU price) and a sample private-offer line item.
- AWS to confirm platform constraints and whether they can include a DocuSign-ready private offer template.
- Acme to confirm whether embeddings should be priced separately or included at generation rate.

Attaching: a one-sheet with proposed line-item fields we'll share internally (acme_priv_offer_line_items.csv).

I’ll follow up with a short mapping sample from our side. If this looks right, can we target a quick sync next week (Wed/Thu)?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

- Is there a recommended conversion you use when vendors map to AWS SKU units?

Subject: Re: AWS Private Offer — proposed mapping table (internal)

Folks — internal draft for how we should map Redwood per-1M-token pricing into AWS private-offer SKU units. Key points and example math below.

Assumptions:
- Redwood invoice unit = 1M tokens (our internal metric).
- AWS private offers must price an integer SKU unit. We'll ship the conversion factor as unit_count = tokens / 1,000,000 so 1 unit = 1M tokens. AWS will enforce integer quantities when buyers purchase; private offer price is applied per unit.
- Minimum price granularity: cents (USD). No sub-cent pricing on AWS Marketplace SKUs.

Example mapping (proposed):
- Redwood list (example): $1,400 / 1M tokens (list for generation-heavy workloads)
- Target Acme negotiated: $1,000 / 1M tokens (per their target)
- AWS SKU unit: 1 unit = 1M tokens -> AWS unit price = $1,000.00

Volume tier suggestion to capture Acme profile:
- Tier A (1–5 units / month): $1,200 per unit
- Tier B (6–15 units / month): $1,000 per unit
- Tier C (16+ units / month): $880 per unit

Notes / risks:
- If AWS requires integer-only tiers or minimums, we should preserve a buffer in our economics to avoid losing margin.
- Embeddings: recommend setting a single blended line item but mark in the PO notes that embeddings are assumed at ~0.6x generation token cost. If Acme insists on separate SKU, we can create a second SKU (embeddings_unit) priced at $600 / 1M tokens.

Action items I will take:
- Attach a draft CSV with line items populated and a sample price column (acme_priv_offer_line_items.csv).
- Run a quick P&L to confirm gross margin at the proposed tiers (Rishi — can you run a margin check on the Tier B price and confirm we maintain target margin?).

Ben
